Full-Stack Developer | React, TypeScript, Node.js

Gothenburg, Sweden | +46 70 555 0808 | oskar.hl@example.com
GitHub: oskarhl-example | Blog: oskar-codes.example.com

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Front-end-focused full-stack developer with 12 years of professional experience building web applications. Strong expertise in React and TypeScript, with hands-on experience developing Node.js services, PostgreSQL-backed features, and mobile applications. Experienced in accessibility improvements, performance optimisation, automated testing, and shipping customer-facing features from design through production. Fluent in English and Swedish.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Frontend: React, TypeScript, JavaScript, Next.js, Angular, AngularJS, Vue, React Native, HTML, CSS, SCSS, Storybook, Redux, React Query
Backend and APIs: Node.js, NestJS, Express, PHP, Laravel, REST, GraphQL
Databases: PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB, Redis, Firebase, Prisma, TypeORM
Testing and delivery: Jest, Playwright, Cypress, React Testing Library, Supertest, GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Docker
Cloud and tools: AWS (ECS, S3, Lambda, SQS, CloudWatch, RDS), Linux, Figma, Jira, Confluence, Sentry, Datadog, Unleash
Other: Web accessibility (WCAG 2.1 AA), A/B testing, BankID, Agile/Scrum

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

Full-Stack Developer | Älvgrind Fintech AB | Gothenburg
2021–Present
- Develop customer-facing onboarding features in React and TypeScript, alongside Node.js services built with NestJS and PostgreSQL.
- Built a BankID identity-verification flow, including QR-code and same-device journeys, error handling, and retries. A/B testing and rollout improved onboarding conversion from 61% to 74%.
- Built a secure document-upload workflow using S3 presigned URLs, ClamAV scanning in Lambda, and SQS status updates recorded in PostgreSQL.
- Helped incrementally migrate the onboarding backend from Express to NestJS, moving routes behind the same API gateway.
- Improved mobile frontend performance through code splitting, image optimisation, and dependency and charting-library replacements; reduced mobile LCP from 4.1 seconds to 1.9 seconds.
- Fixed accessibility issues in the onboarding flow to WCAG 2.1 AA and contributed to design work with designers in Figma.
- Migrated the frontend from Create React App to Vite and contribute to automated testing and production support, including an on-call rotation.
- Maintained a GraphQL backend-for-frontend with another developer; worked with feature flags and GitHub Actions.
- Served as acting team lead for four months in 2024, supporting one-to-ones and sprint planning. Interviewed approximately 30 candidates.
- The onboarding team received the internal Customer Impact Award in 2023.

Developer | Sjöbris Digital Agency AB | Gothenburg
2018–2021
- Built websites and web applications for approximately 25 clients across retail, transport, municipal, and sports sectors using React, Angular, Vue, Node.js, PHP, and WordPress.
- Served as project tech lead and developed most of a React Native ferry-ticket app in a two-developer team. The app supported ticket purchase and offline display and reached approximately 50,000 downloads.
- Built client backends with Node.js/Express and Laravel, and worked with MySQL, MongoDB, and Firebase.
- Set up GitLab CI for the agency, replacing a manual FTP-based deployment workflow.

Web Developer | Nordkust Media AB | Gothenburg
2014–2018
- Developed newspaper websites and an article editor using PHP, jQuery, AngularJS, and MySQL.
- Implemented paywall integration and configured Varnish caching.
- Performed Linux server administration on Ubuntu.

Freelance Developer / Student
2012–2014
- Built websites for local clients, including a bakery and two bands, using PHP, jQuery, and WordPress.

EDUCATION
Bachelor of Computer Science | West Coast University College (Högskola), Gothenburg | 2011–2014

ADDITIONAL EXPERIENCE
- Mentor at a coding bootcamp in Gothenburg, 2019–2020.
- Speaker at a local JavaScript meetup in 2022: “Migrating Express to NestJS without stopping the world.”
- Personal home-automation integrations: built two small Home Assistant integrations in Python, published on GitHub.

LANGUAGES
Swedish: Native | English: Fluent | Arabic: Spoken at home; limited writing | German: Basic, school-level

REFERENCES
Available on request.

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, well-structured CV with clear progression from web developer to full-stack developer, relevant technical breadth, and several quantified achievements. The current Älvgrind role is particularly effective: the BankID conversion increase, mobile LCP improvement, 50,000-app-download result, migration work, and acting team-lead experience create credible impact. The document is professional and substantially more focused than the original candidate information. A few bullets could be more precise about testing and Git-based delivery, and some claims currently describe responsibilities broadly rather than showing the specific tools or outcomes used.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV uses standard, ATS-friendly headings, chronological experience, plain-text contact details, and searchable technology keywords including React, TypeScript, Node.js, NestJS, PostgreSQL, Jest, Playwright, AWS, Docker, Storybook, accessibility, and A/B testing. There are no problematic tables, graphics, icons, or unusual formatting. ATS alignment would improve if the experience section explicitly connected Jest and Playwright to automated testing and named Git-based workflows rather than relying mainly on GitHub Actions and GitLab CI. The CV also does not explicitly contain the terms semantic HTML, responsive layouts, authentication, OWASP Top 10, GDPR, or health-data privacy; these should not be added unless supported by the candidate's actual experience.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document is a very strong match for the core engineering role. It clearly shows well over two years of React and TypeScript experience, Node.js with both Express and NestJS, PostgreSQL and other SQL databases, AWS, Docker, accessibility work, automated-testing tools, design collaboration, Storybook, and A/B testing. The BankID identity-verification flow and secure document-upload workflow provide relevant evidence of authentication and security-conscious engineering, although they do not establish explicit OWASP Top 10 awareness. Next.js is correctly included, with the original information clarifying that it was used for marketing-page SSR. The CV does not show healthcare or wellness experience, explicit health-data privacy or GDPR work, explicit semantic HTML or responsive-layout experience, or German/Croatian customer-facing fluency. It also does not establish the requested willingness to learn health-data privacy requirements. These are candidate-profile gaps rather than defects that can be fixed through wording.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR, HIGH-VALUE IMPROVEMENTS:
1. In the current Älvgrind Fintech AB experience section, replace the broad bullet "Migrated the frontend from Create React App to Vite and contribute to automated testing and production support, including an on-call rotation" with a more ATS-specific version such as: "Migrated the frontend from Create React App to Vite; contributed to automated testing with Jest and Playwright, GitHub Actions delivery, and production support through an on-call rotation." This uses tools already supported by the candidate information and makes the testing and Git-based workflow evidence easier to identify.

2. In the Technical Skills section, change the heading "Testing and delivery" to "Testing, Git and delivery" and list the supported workflow terms as: "Jest, Playwright, Cypress, React Testing Library, Supertest, GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Docker." This improves keyword retrieval without adding unsupported technologies or experience.

3. In the Professional Summary, change "hands-on experience developing Node.js services, PostgreSQL-backed features, and mobile applications" to "hands-on experience developing Node.js services with NestJS and Express, PostgreSQL-backed features, and React Native mobile applications." This more directly mirrors the job description while remaining fully supported by the candidate information.

4. In the current Älvgrind experience section, revise "Built a BankID identity-verification flow" to "Built a BankID identity-verification flow with QR-code and same-device journeys, error handling, and retries." The existing CV contains these details elsewhere in the same role, and including them in the achievement bullet makes the authentication experience more visible to both recruiters and ATS screening.

Claims the sources (the candidate's own material; for the employer, the job ad and company research) do not support:
- contribute to automated testing

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, polished CV with clear chronology, relevant technical breadth, credible ownership, and excellent quantified outcomes. The current role is particularly persuasive: the 61% to 74% conversion improvement, 4.1s to 1.9s mobile LCP reduction, BankID integration, secure document upload, and Express-to-NestJS migration demonstrate meaningful full-stack impact. The acting team-lead experience, mentoring, design collaboration, and production support also add useful seniority signals. The main content weakness is that automated testing and Git-based workflows appear primarily in the skills list rather than as demonstrated delivery activities. The skills section is also broad, so the most relevant capabilities could be prioritized more strongly for this role.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV uses ATS-friendly standard headings, plain text formatting, consistent dates, and keyword-rich technology categories. It should parse reliably, and its AI screening probability is high because React, TypeScript, Node.js, NestJS, PostgreSQL, AWS, Docker, Jest, Playwright, Storybook, accessibility, and A/B testing are all clearly visible. Add the standalone keyword "Git" because the CV currently shows GitHub Actions and GitLab CI but does not explicitly name Git. The document would also screen more strongly if automated testing were labeled as unit and end-to-end testing rather than only listing test tools. Avoid adding unsupported keywords such as OWASP Top 10, GDPR, WCAG 2.2, or healthcare experience.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: Alignment is very strong for the core engineering requirements. The CV clearly demonstrates substantially more than two years of React and TypeScript experience, Node.js and SQL backend work, accessibility improvements, AWS and Docker, Storybook, Next.js, A/B testing, regulated fintech/KYC work, and fluent English. The fintech, identity-verification, secure document-upload, and BankID work are relevant adjacent experience for a privacy-conscious healthcare product. Automated testing and Git-based delivery are present but could be made more explicit. The document does not establish OWASP Top 10 awareness, semantic HTML or responsive-layout experience in the ad's exact terms, or willingness to learn health-data privacy requirements. It also does not show healthcare experience; these are alignment gaps rather than CV-writing defects. German is listed as basic and therefore is only a limited match for customer-facing conversations.
critique.improvement_instructions:
HIGH PRIORITY — In the Technical Skills section, change the heading "Testing, Git and delivery" to "Automated Testing and Git-Based Delivery" and make the contents more ATS-explicit: "Jest, Playwright, Cypress, React Testing Library, Supertest; Git, GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Docker." This uses technologies already present in the original candidate information and makes the unit, end-to-end, and Git workflow keywords easier to identify.

HIGH PRIORITY — In the current Älvgrind Fintech experience, add a concise testing/delivery bullet based only on work the candidate can substantiate, for example: "Used Jest and Playwright within GitHub Actions-based delivery for automated test coverage and release confidence." Do not add claims about specific test types, coverage percentages, or ownership that the candidate cannot verify.

MEDIUM PRIORITY — In the BankID bullet under Älvgrind, make the security relevance more explicit without claiming OWASP expertise. For example, change the opening to: "Implemented a BankID authentication and identity-verification flow with QR-code and same-device journeys, error handling, and retries." This more directly matches the job's authentication and web-security requirement while remaining supported by the candidate information.

MEDIUM PRIORITY — In the Professional Summary, add the existing testing and delivery evidence so it is not buried in the skills list. For example, revise the final part to: "Experienced in accessibility improvements, mobile performance optimisation, automated testing with Jest and Playwright, Git-based delivery, and shipping customer-facing features from design through production." Keep the wording limited to tools and activities supported by the original information; do not add OWASP, GDPR, or health-data claims.

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, well-structured CV with clear senior-level experience, credible technical depth, useful metrics, and relevant end-to-end delivery examples. The strongest evidence includes the 61% to 74% onboarding conversion improvement, mobile LCP reduction from 4.1 seconds to 1.9 seconds, the 50,000-download React Native app, and the Express-to-NestJS migration. The document is professional and substantially more focused than the original candidate information. Minor weaknesses are that some job-relevant concepts are listed but not explicitly demonstrated, particularly semantic HTML, responsive layouts, and security fundamentals. The skills section is also broad, so the most relevant capabilities could be prioritized more clearly for this patient-facing engineering role.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: ATS compatibility is high. The CV uses conventional section headings, reverse-chronological experience, plain text formatting, recognizable technology names, and strong keyword coverage for React, TypeScript, Node.js, NestJS, PostgreSQL, Jest, Playwright, GitHub Actions, AWS, Docker, Storybook, Next.js, accessibility, and A/B testing. The heading "Automated Testing and Git-Based Delivery" is especially useful for keyword matching. AI screening probability is high because the CV clearly connects technologies to delivered outcomes rather than relying only on a keyword inventory. To improve matching further, explicitly connect the existing BankID work to authentication and security, and use the ad's exact wording where supported, such as "end-to-end tests," "design reviews," and "sprint planning." Do not add OWASP, healthcare privacy, semantic HTML, or responsive-layout claims unless they are factually supported.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document is a very strong match for the core engineering requirements. It shows substantially more than the required two years of React and TypeScript experience, backend development with Node.js and SQL databases, automated unit and end-to-end testing, Git-based workflows, accessibility work, AWS, Docker, Next.js, Storybook, and A/B testing. The fintech/KYC context and identity-verification and document-upload work provide relevant evidence of working with authentication and sensitive customer data in a regulated environment. The main evidence gaps are explicit knowledge of OWASP Top 10, semantic HTML and responsive layouts, and health-data privacy requirements; these are candidate-evidence gaps rather than defects that can be solved by rewriting. The CV also does not demonstrate German or Croatian customer-facing fluency, although German is only a nice-to-have and is accurately described as basic.
critique.improvement_instructions:
1. In the Professional Summary, replace the general sentence beginning "Experienced in accessibility improvements" with a more job-aligned version that uses only supported evidence: "Experienced in accessible, performance-focused customer-facing web applications, automated unit and end-to-end testing with Jest and Playwright, Git-based delivery, authentication and secure document-upload workflows, and shipping features from design through production." This makes the existing authentication and security-related experience easier for ATS and recruiters to identify without claiming OWASP expertise.

2. In the Technical Skills section, change "Automated Testing and Git-Based Delivery" to "Automated Testing and Git-Based Workflows" and retain the existing tools. This more closely matches the job ad's wording while remaining truthful.

3. For this role, prioritize React, TypeScript, HTML, CSS, accessibility, Node.js, NestJS, PostgreSQL, Jest, Playwright, GitHub Actions, AWS, Docker, Storybook, Next.js, and A/B testing before older or less relevant technologies such as AngularJS, PHP, and Firebase.
